📌 Tehran, IRNA – The commander of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps (IRGC) Ground Force has warned that any further miscalculations by Iran’s adversaries would accelerate their expulsion from the region and contribute to the destruction of Israel.

Brigadier General Mohammad Karami made the remarks in a message issued on Wednesday to mark the National Day of Struggle Against Global Arrogance.
​
Karami said the continuation of hostile and brutal actions by Iran’s enemies would only lead to further Iranian victories and greater national pride, while hastening the expulsion of foreign powers from the region and the collapse of the Israeli regime.
​
He said the United States’ conduct toward Iran over recent decades, from its opposition to the nationalization of the oil industry and its role in the 1953 coup to various plots following the 1979 Islamic Revolution, reflected the hegemonic nature of Washington’s policies.
​
Karami also cited the imposition of two wars against Iran over the past one and a half years and the “coup-like unrest” of January 2026, saying these actions were aimed at forcing Iran into submission, overthrowing its government and ultimately taking control of the country.
​
He said these efforts had consistently failed because of the resistance and strong response of the Iranian people, as well as the sacrifices of those martyred in defending the country.
​
The commander stressed that Iran’s adversaries had come to understand that repeating their strategic miscalculations and continuing their hostile conduct would produce no outcome other than further Iranian successes and the accelerated withdrawal of their forces from the region.

📡 Iran protests IMO’s biased reports on shipping security

📌 London, IRNA – The Islamic Republic of Iran has criticized the International Maritime Organization (IMO) biased reports on the shipping crisis, stressing that seafarer protection should not be selective and that the difficult conditions facing Iranian seafarers must also be addressed.

The Iranian delegation at the 138th session of the IMO Council in London criticized the organization’s incomplete and unbalanced reports on maritime security and seafarer protection, calling for an impartial assessment of threats to maritime safety.
​
The delegation stressed that IMO reports should not overlook the US naval blockade of Iranian ports and military attacks on vessels and the country’s critical maritime safety infrastructure.
​
It also called for the organization's future reports to fairly reflect Iran’s legal positions, supported by documents submitted to Council members.
​
Emphasizing that seafarer protection should not be selective, the Iranian delegation called for equal treatment of all seafarers, regardless of nationality or political differences. In this regard, it raised concerns over the difficult conditions facing Iranian seafarers near Sri Lanka and called for urgent and non-discriminatory action.
​
The Iranian delegation also protested the repetition of allegations against Iran in the IMO Secretary-General’s report, reiterating its rejection of the May resolution adopted by the Maritime Safety Committee as political and legally unfounded.
​
The delegation called for transparent, comprehensive and impartial reporting on maritime threats and urgent protection for affected seafarers, particularly Iranians, holding US and Israeli military aggression and the naval blockade of Iran responsible for the current crisis.
​
The 138th session of the Council is being held in person at the IMO Headquarters, with hybrid facilities for remote participation, from Monday 2 November to Friday 6 November.
